messages:
jess_hansen: Hey team — running into a weird 403 only on /v1/rerank. Embeddings and completions work fine with the same API key we provisioned via SSO. Example curl shows 403. Can someone help?

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX_REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rdr-rerank-1","queries":["q1"],"candidates":["a","b"]}'

jess_hansen: Error body: `\{"error\":\{"type\":\"forbidden\",\"message\":\"missing permission: rerank.write\"\}\}`

support-bot: Thanks for the report, @jess_hansen. I've created ticket CS-7123 and set priority to P2. Related logs have been attached to the ticket.

maya_cs: @jess_hansen can you confirm how that key was created? SSO-provisioned API key or hand-created in Console? Also, do you see any `scopes` metadata in the Console when you view the key?

jess_hansen: Key was created via SSO provisioning (Google Workspace SSO). I don't see a `rerank` scope in the Console UI — only `inference:generate` and `embeddings:read` listed. I can share the provisioning flow if helpful.

leo_oncall: tagging @samir_eng — this could be an SSO role -> token-scope mapping issue we've seen in the past with the new SCIM mapping change. Can you grab the provisioning audit log?

samir_eng: On it. @jess_hansen can you paste the provisioning webhook payload (redact identifiable fields) or the role names assigned in the IdP? Looking for claims like `client_scopes` or `app_roles`.

jess_hansen: Provided minimal payload to the ticket. Role names were: `Redwood-Dev`, `Rerank-Clients` (but I think that second one was only in the IdP group, not mapped during SSO).

samir_eng: I pulled the provisioning log for that timestamp. The IdP sent `groups: [\"Redwood-Dev\", \"Rerank-Clients\"]`, but our SCIM mapper has a bug where group names with a dash are normalized and a conditional rule ignores groups that don't match exact prefix. Result: `Rerank-Clients` got dropped. That explains missing `rerank.write` scope on the generated key.

samir_eng: Repro steps I used locally: 1) Create IdP group `Rerank-Clients` 2) Trigger SSO provisioning 3) Observe generated key via the provisioning endpoint returns scopes: `[\"inference.generate\", \"embeddings.read\"]` (missing `rerank.write`) 4) Check SCIM mapper logs: `Normalized group 'rerankclients' not matched -> skip mapping`

maya_cs: Thanks @samir_eng. Impact? Which customers are affected?

samir_eng: So far only customers that: (a) provisioned keys via the SSO flow since the SCIM mapping change, and (b) used IdP group names containing punctuation/dashes. I scanned the provisioning table and found ~4 keys in prod with similar group names — flagged them in CS-7123.

jess_hansen: Ok — we need a fix and a workaround. Our production app hits rerank at scale, so this is blocking.

samir_eng: Short-term workaround: 1) In Console > API Keys, create a new manual API key and explicitly select `rerank` permission OR 2) Rotate the SSO-provisioned key by re-running provisioning after renaming the IdP group to remove punctuation (eg `RerankClients`). Both valid. I'll put a scripted rollback mapping in the ticket so we can update existing keys if customer allows.

maya_cs: Can we auto-detect affected keys and notify customers? We should proactively reach out if they rely on rerank.

leo_oncall: I can run a query to find keys where `scopes` does not include `rerank.write` but were created by the SSO flow and have `Rerank-` in original provisioning metadata. I'll add a row to the incident docs and ping Growth with a templated message.

ops_incident_bot: Incident page created: https://ops.redwood-internal/incident/CS-7123. Severity P2. Action owner: samir_eng. ETA for hotfix: 6 hours.

samir_eng: Plan: patch SCIM mapper to stop normalizing group names into a single token (fix in `scim-mapper:v1.4.2`), add a migration to re-evaluate recent provisioning events and apply missing mappings, and provide a safe API for CS to grant `rerank.write` to specific keys. I'll post a PR link in ~2h.

jess_hansen: For our customer, we prefer the Console key route (manual create) while you patch. I'll create a new key and swap it in. Any suggested cookie-cutter steps for devs?

maya_cs: Steps for customers/devs: 1) Console -> API keys -> Create key -> enable `rerank` permission (and `inference`/`embeddings` as needed) 2) Swap out the Bearer token in app and test with small batch. 3) Optional: revoke old SSO key after swap. If they can't create manual keys for policy reasons, ask them to rename IdP group to remove punctuation and reprovision.

samir_eng: Follow-up: PR submitted: https://git.internal/pulls/3512. Fix includes unit tests and a migration script. I'll coordinate with infra to deploy to staging, then prod. ETA prod deploy: ~6-8 hours.

maya_cs: I'll email the customer with the workaround & offer to create a Console key for them to swap (if they want CS to do it). Also added a note to CS-7123 to follow up post-deploy to audit all SSO-provisioned keys and rotate if necessary.

jess_hansen: Thanks everyone. Please @mention me in the PR and when the migration runs.

samir_eng: Will do. Also adding a short-term telemetry alert to detect new provisioning events with dropped groups.

leo_oncall: I've started the query to identify affected customers and will attach results to CS-7123.

maya_cs: Closing the thread for now — updating ticket with suggested customer message and workaround steps. Reopen if anything new comes up. :thumbsup:
